title: 4K FXAA Landscape geometry diagnostic
hypothesis: A high-resolution neutral proof can distinguish screen-space aliasing from actual heightfield structure.
technical: 3840 x 2160 capture completed at forced Landscape LOD0.
Neutral geometry diagnosis avoided project-material camouflage.
R16 precision and vertical quantization were not identified as the dominant failure.
visual: Dense herringbone seen in earlier 1080p captures was substantially reduced.
Steep-face stepping/ribbing remained visible, proving that a real geometry/source-resolution limitation still exists.
keep: 4K neutral rider/terrain diagnostic as a debugging technique.
Forced-LOD and anti-aliasing controls for separating renderer artifacts from geometry.
reject: Treating all earlier terrain artifacts as 16-bit quantization or fixing them with blanket smoothing.
learnings: Part of the failure was screen-space aliasing, but not all of it.
A green authoring run does not imply acceptable rider-camera geometry.
next: Use dedicated local geometry/corridor treatment for inspectable steep surfaces.
